byrne.name: Oliver Byrne
byrne.role: Irish Civil Engineer, Surveyor & Mathematical Author
byrne.summary: Professor of Mathematics at the College for Civil Engineers, Putney, and Her Majesty's Surveyor of the Falkland Islands; conceived the pointer-free four-color visual language of the 1847 Elements of Euclid to eliminate alphabetic vertex indirection.

euclid.name: Euclid of Alexandria
euclid.role: Ancient Greek Geometer & Author of the Stoicheia (Elements)
euclid.summary: Compiled the thirteen books of the Elements, Books I–VI of which constitute the planar geometric, algebraic, and proportional canon rendered in color by Oliver Byrne.

whittingham.name: Charles Whittingham the Younger
whittingham.role: Master Printer of the Chiswick Press
whittingham.summary: Nephew of Charles Whittingham the Elder; executed the extraordinary four-run Caslon letterpress and relief woodblock registration (red, blue, yellow, black) that made Byrne's 1847 Euclid a landmark of Victorian bookmaking.

pickering.name: William Pickering
pickering.summary: Publisher of the Aldine Poets and partner of Charles Whittingham; financed and published Byrne's 1847 coloured Euclid shortly before the Great Exhibition of 1851.

simson.name: Robert Simson
simson.role: Scottish Mathematician & Professor of Mathematics at Glasgow
simson.summary: Published the standard 1756 Latin and English edition of Euclid's Elements (Books I–VI, XI–XII), whose numbering of 35 Definitions, 3 Postulates, and 12 Axioms Oliver Byrne adopted directly.

demorgan.name: Augustus De Morgan
demorgan.role: British Mathematician & Pioneer of Relational Logic
demorgan.summary: Professor at University College London who dismissed Byrne's coloured Euclid as an eccentric curiosity in A Budget of Paradoxes, missing its anticipation of typed visual token languages.

pestalozzi.name: Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi
pestalozzi.summary: Championed Anschauung (direct sensory-spatial intuition prior to verbal symbols) in elementary mathematics education—explicitly invoked by Byrne's pedagogical philosophy in the 1847 Introduction.

horace.name: Quintus Horatius Flaccus (Horace)
horace.summary: Quoted by Oliver Byrne on p. viii of the 1847 Introduction (Ars Poetica 180–181: Segnius irritant animos demissa per aurem / Quam quae sunt oculis subjecta fidelibus) to justify ocular over auditory/verbal demonstration.

eudoxus.name: Eudoxus of Cnidus
eudoxus.summary: Architect of the general theory of proportion in Book V (Definition 5), which Byrne translates into a four-shape, four-color symbolic algebra.

proclus.name: Proclus Lycius (Diadochus)
proclus.role: Neoplatonic Philosopher & Commentator on Euclid Book I
proclus.summary: Codified the six canonical parts of a Euclidean proposition (protasis, ekthesis, diorismos, kataskeue, apodeixis, symperasma) that govern Byrne's block layout.

heath.name: Sir Thomas Little Heath
heath.role: Historian of Greek Mathematics & Translator of Euclid
heath.summary: Author of the definitive 1908 Cambridge edition digitized in geometor/euclid, serving as the classical alphabetic baseline in our 3-way Rosetta analysis.

hoenen.name: Petrus Hubertus Jacobus Hoenen, S.J.
hoenen.role: Philosopher of Geometry & Author of De Noetica Geometriae
hoenen.summary: Analyzed how universal geometric necessity is grasped directly within the concrete spatial phantasma (geometor/hoenen)—the exact epistemological principle materialized by Byrne's colored plates.

mclean.name: Ruari McLean
mclean.role: Scottish Typographer & Historian of Victorian Book Design
mclean.summary: Rehabilitated Oliver Byrne and Charles Whittingham in Victorian Book Design and Colour Printing (1963), calling the 1847 Euclid 'one of the oddest and most beautiful books of the whole century'.

tufte.name: Edward Rolf Tufte
tufte.summary: Highlighted Byrne's 1847 Euclid in Envisioning Information (1990) as a masterclass in small multiples, micro/macro color encoding, and elimination of figure-to-text eye-scanning latency.

rougeux.name: Nicholas Rougeux
rougeux.summary: Created the celebrated December 2018 interactive web restoration of Byrne's Euclid (c82.net/euclid) and authored 'Making of Byrne's Euclid', demonstrating interactive shape-highlighting for modern readers.
